gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns a variable mismatch in the secproxthm lemma: the hypothesis quantifies f while the conclusion and later instantiation use ψ. ISSUE-003 instead concerns applying convergence theorems to operators whose averaging constants may exceed 1/2. These are different mathematical subjects and defects, despite both involving formal hypotheses and downstream theorem use.

The gold defect is that theorem item (i) writes a nonnegative series bound by +∞, which fails to state the strict finiteness needed by the proof. ISSUE-004 instead diagnoses the separate empirical inference that finitely many plotted partial sums cannot certify convergence of the infinite series. It does not recognize the formal omission in the theorem item or its repair to <+∞.

Both identify the same defect: finite partial sums shown in the denoising experiment cannot establish convergence of the corresponding infinite series, so the hypothesis of convergerate and its rate guarantee are not certified. ISSUE-004 also gives the appropriate limitation of the empirical claim.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Finite experimental partial sums cannot verify convergence or summability of the unobserved infinite tail, so the conditional rate theorem cannot be categorically applied to the denoising runs.

component_coverage.gold_component: The plot contains only finitely many partial sums and therefore cannot verify convergence of the infinite parameter-difference series or establish the theorem's rate hypothesis.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 explicitly states that the figure shows finitely many partial sums, that apparent stabilization cannot establish convergence of the infinite series, and that the rate claim is consequently unsupported; its repair limits the claim to boundedness over the tested range.
